title: How to Prepare an Email Welcome Series Before Hiring
h1: How to prepare an email welcome series before hiring
description: Prepare a welcome email series: goal, audience, number of emails, timing, offers, tone, tracking, consent and what to ask a freelancer to set up.
intro: A welcome series is a short run of automatic emails sent when someone joins your list or makes a first purchase. These emails are read more than almost any other message you send, which makes them a valuable place to build trust and guide people toward a first action. A freelancer can write and set them up, but you need to decide the goal and share what makes your business worth remembering. This article explains how to prepare.

faq.q: How many emails should a welcome series have?
faq.a: Many series use three to five emails over one to two weeks. The right number depends on your product and how much people need to learn.

faq.q: What should the first email do?
faq.a: Thank the person, deliver what you promised, such as a discount or guide, and tell them what to expect.

faq.q: Should the emails include a discount?
faq.a: Only if it fits your margins and brand. Some businesses prefer to build trust first and offer a discount later.

faq.q: What do I need to supply?
faq.a: Brand details, key products or services, customer questions, reviews, links and any offer details.

faq.q: How do I know it works?
faq.a: Track opens, clicks and, most importantly, the actions you want, such as first purchases or bookings.
